questions.prompt: What does `TTL key` return for a key that exists but has no expiry set?
questions.explanation: TTL returns -1 when the key exists but has no expiry, and -2 when the key does not exist. A positive number is the seconds remaining.

questions.prompt: How does Redis expire keys? Select all that apply.

options.text: Passively — an expired key is removed when a client next accesses it
Actively — a background cycle samples keys with TTLs and removes expired ones
With a precise per-key timer that fires the exact millisecond the TTL hits zero
A read will never return a value that has already expired

questions.explanation: Expiration is passive plus active (eventual, not a precise timer), but reads never return an expired value — it's logically gone the moment it expires.

questions.prompt: You run `SET k "v" EX 100`, then later `SET k "v2"`. What is the TTL of k afterward?

options.text: -1 (the TTL was cleared by the plain SET)

questions.explanation: A full-replacement SET clears any existing TTL. To keep it you'd use SET k "v2" KEEPTTL or re-apply EXPIRE.

questions.prompt: How is expiration different from eviction?

options.text: They are two names for the same thing
Expiration removes a key when its own TTL is due; eviction removes keys under memory pressure per a policy
Expiration only happens in Redis Cluster; eviction only on a single node
Eviction applies only to keys that have a TTL

questions.explanation: A TTL is a deadline you set on one key; eviction is triggered by hitting maxmemory and can remove keys (even ones without TTLs) according to the configured policy.

questions.prompt: The command that removes a key's TTL so it stops expiring is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: PERSIST removes the expiry, leaving the key in place until it is explicitly deleted (TTL then returns -1).

questions.prompt: Which single command sets a value AND a 60-second expiry atomically?

options.text: SET key value; EXPIRE key 60 (two commands)

questions.explanation: SET with the EX option sets the value and the relative expiry in one atomic command, avoiding a window where the key exists without a TTL.
